record.paper_title: Semigroups of rational functions: some problems and conjectures
record.original_question: Let P be a non-special rational function of degree at least two. Is there an integer s ≥ 1 such that the semigroup C_∞(P), defined as the union of the commuting semigroups C(P^{∘k}) over all k ≥ 1, is exactly equal to C(P^{∘s})?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.2. Let P be a non-special rational function of degree at least two. Then C∞(P) = C(P^{∘s}) for some s ≥ 1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P$ be a rational function of degree at least two viewed as a self-map of the Riemann sphere $\widehat{\mathbb{C}}$. For a rational function $F$, write $F^{\circ k}$ for the $k$-fold iterate $F\circ F\circ\cdots\circ F$, and define the commuting semigroup
$$C(F) \;=\; \{\,G:\widehat{\mathbb{C}}\to\widehat{\mathbb{C}} \text{ rational} : F\circ G = G\circ F\,\}.$$
Since $C(F)\subseteq C(F^{\circ k})$ for every $k\ge 1$, set
$$C_\infty(P) \;=\; \bigcup_{k\ge 1} C(P^{\circ k}).$$
A rational function of degree at least two is called special if it is conjugate (by a Möbius transformation) either to a power map $z\mapsto z^n$, to a Chebyshev polynomial $\pm T_n$, or to a Lattès map (a map induced by an endomorphism of an elliptic curve via a finite quotient). Otherwise it is called non-special.

Question: Assume that $P$ is non-special. Does there exist an integer $s\ge 1$ such that
$$C_\infty(P) \;=\; C(P^{\circ s})\,?$$
artifact.status_search_result: The stabilization $C_\infty(P)=C(P^{\circ s})$ has been established by Pakovich for the subclass of tame rational functions (which form a proper subclass of non-special rational functions), as part of his work on tame rational functions and amenable semigroups. However, the general case of arbitrary non-special rational functions of degree at least two does not appear to be settled in the literature found.

status_evidence.title: On amenable semigroups of rational functions (Pakovich)
status_evidence.snippet: If S is tame, then every F ∈ S has degree at least two and is not special, and C∞(F) = C(P), where P = F◦s for some s ≥ 1.
status_evidence.claim: Stabilization is proved for tame rational functions, a subclass of non-special ones.

status_evidence.title: Tame rational functions: Decompositions of iterates and orbit intersections
status_evidence.snippet: For a tame rational function P, the semigroup C∞(P) coincides with C(P◦k) for some k ≥ 1; described as a stabilization result of independent interest.
status_evidence.claim: Stabilization is known in the tame case, leaving the general non-special case unresolved.
